campaignStructure.chapters: Prologue: World of Chaos + 16 numbered chapters (I-XVI) = 17 total. Chapter titles reconstructed from partial sources, medium confidence on exact wording.
bosses: The Masked Lumen / young time-displaced Balder (recurring, multi-chapter)
Alraune (Ch. XI: Inferno and Its Ruler, two-phase)
Loptr/Aesir (final boss, Ch. XVI: Sovereign Power — exact in-game display name unconfirmed, avoid quoting 'Loptr' or 'Aesir' directly in trophy text)
campaignStructure.notPlayableAsBoss: Loki is a companion ally, never fought.
campaignStructure.difficulty: Very Easy, Easy, Normal, Hard, ∞ Climax (hardest — drops the 'Non-Stop' prefix used in Bayonetta 1). Same sequential unlock pattern (Normal→Hard→∞ Climax).
campaignStructure.verseRanking: Same Stone→Pure Platinum six-tier system as Bayonetta 1, confirmed present (high confidence via Wikipedia direct quote + community point-value breakdown), reviewable via Menu > Play History.
campaignStructure.ending: Single linear ending; post-credits epilogue shows young Balder returning to his time, corrupted — seeds the original Bayonetta's plot.
campaignStructure.optionalContent: Lost Chapter: Witch Trials — 5 bonus chapters (Witch Trial I-V), unlocked after completing Story Mode once. Witch Trial V includes a double-boss fight (Alraune + Young Loptr). Exact unlock trigger (which difficulty/rank) unconfirmed.

collectiblesAndSystems.weapons: 10-12 total depending on source (discrepancy unresolved): Love Is Blue (default), Rakshasa, Alruna (story unlock, defeat Alraune), Kafka, Chernobog, Salamandra, Takemikazuchi, Undine, Chain Chomp (Mario-themed, Bayonetta-2-exclusive), Rodin (secret superboss reward via Platinum Ticket).
collectiblesAndSystems.umbranCrows: 20 total, scattered across ~11 of 16 chapters. Reward was Miiverse stamps — dead since Nov 2017 shutdown; the underlying pickup itself is presumably still trackable, though the exact tracking menu/screen for Bayonetta 2 specifically is unconfirmed.
collectiblesAndSystems.bewitchments: ~30 in-fiction challenge conditions, reportedly combining with the 20 Crows into '50 Umbran Tears of Blood' total — mechanic/tracking screen unconfirmed (medium-low confidence).
collectiblesAndSystems.muspelheim: Bayonetta 2's Alfheim-equivalent hidden challenge verses. No confirmed total count across all chapters (only fragmentary per-chapter data).
collectiblesAndSystems.noGlobalStatsScreen: No confirmed dedicated Records/Statistics menu (playtime, lifetime Halos, combo records) — every relevant primary source was blocked this session. Do not design a cumulative-currency or playtime trophy.
collectiblesAndSystems.missables: Same as Bayonetta 1 — full Chapter Select replay available indefinitely; nothing permanently missable. Pure Platinum needs a single clean continuous run of a chapter.

costumesAndDLC.noDLCConfirmed: Director Yusuke Hashimoto confirmed at E3 2014 there is NO DLC for Bayonetta 2 — everything, including all Nintendo costumes, ships on-disc. High confidence, corroborated by two independent scouts and VGChartz's extras page showing none.
costumesAndDLC.nintendoCostumes: 5 on-disc costumes via Super Mirror 64-2 (100,000 Halos each): Pilot Suit (Fox McCloud/Star Fox), Mushroom Kingdom Princess (Peach), Sarasaland Princess (Daisy), Galactic Bounty Hunter (Samus), Hero of Hyrule (Link). A second tier (Super Mirror 64, 'Legacy Hair' variants) requires beating Story Mode on Hard or higher. No Palutena or Wonder Red costume exists (ruled out this session).
costumesAndDLC.otherCostumes: Non-Nintendo Super Mirror 2 line (Gekka, Schoolgirl, Police Woman, Witch Apprentice, Metal Witch, Dress) and ported Bayonetta-1-style costumes (A Witch With No Memories, The Last Witch, Old, Nun) available via Halos purchase, some gated behind difficulty completion.
costumesAndDLC.amiibo: Optional instant-unlock shortcut for costumes already obtainable via Halos — never required, never exclusive content. Not a valid trophy basis.
costumesAndDLC.designFlag: The user's request to treat 'Switch bonus content' as a DLC-style list runs into the same problem as Bayonetta 1: costumes are already Wii U base content, not Switch-exclusive.

wiiUVsSwitch.confirmedSwitchExclusive: Tag Climax (the online co-op/competitive mode) gained LOCAL wireless 2-console co-op on Switch. Wii U's Tag Climax was online-only. This is the one genuine, functional Switch-only change found — but it's a connectivity mode, not new unlockable content, and thin material for a standalone trophy (at most one trophy: 'play Tag Climax locally').
wiiUVsSwitch.amiiboSupport: amiibo scanning itself is a Switch-exclusive feature (Wii U had none for this game), but only as a shortcut to existing Halos-purchasable content — not new content.
wiiUVsSwitch.onlineStatus: Wii U's Nintendo Network (needed for Tag Climax online matchmaking) permanently shut down April 8, 2024. No trophy should require live online Tag Climax on Wii U going forward.
wiiUVsSwitch.designImplication: As with Bayonetta 1, there isn't enough substantive Switch-exclusive content here to justify a full separate DLC-style list under Rule 14 (validate.mjs flags <5 trophies as too thin to stand alone). The one real difference (local Tag Climax co-op) could at most be a single note or a single bonus trophy folded into the base list — needs a checkpoint decision.
